newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia aims for half world oils market-minister.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia aims for half world oils market-minister.

text.p: Malaysia aims to take over the world oil and fats market by investing in plantations in foreign countries, relocating refineries to growing markets and marketing palm oil for non-traditional usages, Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik said on Thursday.
"We should be taking over the oil and fats market," the national news agency Bernama quoted Lim as saying at a forum organised by the Malaysian Strategic Research Centre.

Malaysia, the world's largest producer and exporter of palm oil, had two factors in its favour in seeking to dominate the oils market, he said. Palm oil has a much wider variety of usages than competitors such as soya bean or red seed oil and there was greater economies of scale in its production.
"It takes only three years for the (oil palm) tree to mature and you can harvest the crop for 27 years," Lim said.
"Malaysia has no more land or labour to grow palm oil hence we have to go abroad (to places) like Indonesia, Cambodia, Southern Philippines, South Pacific Islands, latin America and Africa," he said.
Malaysia has already invested about 1 billion ringgit in palm oil plantations in Indonesia, he said.

Lim also stressed the need for palm oil producers to go downstream into toiletries related products by establishing joint ventures with popular brand names and also find industrial uses for non-edible oil.
"You do not buy over the company. Buy a small stake. Hold a director's position in the company and use their extensive retail chain," Bernama quoted him as saying.
